name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Keep the Designs tab pure: designs only, live previews, taste-ranked

name: Reel
text: Adopt the PCIe-attached validator: a $50 ARM board with direct NVMe access. It’s the only option that guarantees real-time transcript validation without latency or cloud dependency, keeping the Designs tab pure. The trade-off is a one-time hardware cost and setup effort, but it eliminates ongoing Deepgram fees and avoids the slower, less reliable path of using Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite for validation.

name: Scriv
text: The PCIe-attached validator isn’t the only way to keep the Designs tab pure—Deepgram’s real-time API could validate transcripts live without hardware, trading cloud dependency for zero setup. The real risk is the ARM board’s firmware trust: if NVMe lies, the validator fails silently, and we still need a fallback. Settle it by running a side-by-side test: compare Deepgram’s API latency and accuracy against the PCIe validator’s raw NVMe reads under worst-case load.
